generator.program.note: The lineage's own program (growth plan G2.3a), on the herb base: it gives the values its species leave unset, which the herb program gave as defaults until then.

traits.perianth.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 291: perianth dichlamydeous, 5 to 8 often petaloid sepals and few to many (rarely no) petals, parts spirally arranged in usually two series; Floral Diagrams p. 137 also allows an undifferentiated spiral perianth (P 1 to many).

traits.flower_merosity.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 291: Simpson's formula: sepals 5 to 8, rarely 3 (Floral Diagrams p. 137-139: Fibonacci counts such as 5 sepals and 8 nectar-leaf petals).

traits.stamens.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 291: stamens usually many, spiral and centripetal (Floral Diagrams p. 137: 5 to many). Book writes ∞ (numerous); 200 is our stand-in for the upper bound and 20 for 'numerous' with no stated lower bound.

traits.carpels.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 291: gynoecium usually of many free carpels, sometimes one to few. Book writes ∞; 50 is our stand-in for the upper bound.

traits.hypanthium.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 291: Simpson states a hypanthium is absent; flowers hypogynous.

traits.note: Plants of the World Online's account of the family, as search results quote it (the page itself was not read): flowers usually actinomorphic, less commonly zygomorphic (as in Aconitum); sepals (3-)5 to 8, often petaloid; stamens numerous, usually spirally arranged; carpels one to many, usually free; ovary superior.

traits.woodiness.note: Hutchinson (vol. 1, 2nd ed., 1959), families 249 Ranunculaceae (buttercups, anemones, Clematis) and 248 Helleboraceae (hellebores, columbines, larkspurs), which APG joins as Ranunculaceae: mostly perennial or annual herbs with basal and alternate leaves, a few shrubs or climbers (Clematis) with opposite leaves; stipules absent or only sheathing bases of the leaf stalk; fruit a cluster of dry achenes in the first, follicles in the second.

traits.rosette.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Ranunculaceae as that work draws it, there coded together with Hydrastidaceae: whether the leaves gather in rosettes (character 22), coded often a basal rosette, often no rosette. Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py with character 21 added); states the authors do not qualify, side by side, read as often.

traits.life_span.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Ranunculaceae as that work draws it, there coded together with Hydrastidaceae: the herbs' life form (character 21), coded often annual, often biennial, often perennial. Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py with character 21 added); states the authors do not qualify, side by side, read as often.

traits.zygomorphy.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data), family Ranunculaceae with Hydrastidaceae: its irregular flowers are of no named kind (pea flower, two lips, orchid lip), read from the coded corolla symmetry (spec-rework/b1/delta): zygomorphy other. Its flowers are not mostly zygomorphic, so a plant of it states its own symmetry; one that is zygomorphic draws this kind, and one stating none is drawn regular.

traits.leaf_division.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data), family Ranunculaceae with Hydrastidaceae, which APG and WCVP join to it (their extra states read as sometimes): leaves simple often, compound often; the simple blade dissected often, none often, lobed sometimes; lobes or leaflets palmate often, pinnate often. Read from the coded leaf form and dissection by script (spec-rework/b1/delta). The simple leaves are mostly palmately lobed or divided (Ranunculus, Aconitum, Delphinium), the compound ones ternate or pinnate (Clematis, Thalictrum).

traits.inflorescence.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 291, 292, family Ranunculaceae: inflorescence cyme or solitary; read as {"cyme": "often", "solitary": "often"}.
